correctness.rationale: The proof explicitly defines Euclidean isotonic projection and a separate four-vertex Sobolev error norm. Every composition of four is an open pooling cell; the exact global Lipschitz modulus equals the maximum of eight Q-induced block-average matrix norms. The generalized determinants were checked as bivariate polynomial identities, not only sampled numerically, by 5x5 degree-bounded rational interpolation. Symbolic rational differences prove only the (2,2)/(1,2,1) and (1,3)/(3,1) families can maximize, with a unique gamma=1/2 crossing and derivative jump 1/126. Two actual pairs give exact ratios 31/27 and 143/142; general exact attainment follows from spectral directions inside open cells. No extension to longer chains is inferred.

value.rationale: Four points are the smallest natural isotonic chain permitting competition between separated double pooling and a single triple pool. A unique sharp coupling transition at 1/2, derivative cusp, explicit maximizer cells and actual attaining pairs provide an exact sensitivity benchmark for monotone regression under gradient-sensitive error norms. This is more than an ordinary yes/no contraction test and specifies a useful first phase transition without asserting a larger-dimensional result.
